text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> prod: embeddings-api (us-west-2) high 5xx rate (threshold breached). alert_id=emb-5xx-5201. routed to oncall-jay :rotating_light:

oncall-jay: Ack, I'm on it. Any initial signal on what changed?

eng-maya: We just cut encoder-service:v2 to ~30% of traffic via rollout and a canary drain started ~2m before the pager. Canaries show CrashLoopBackOff on encoder-replicaset-2. Logs show liveness failing immediately.

eng-maya: kubectl -n prod logs encoder-5b7f -c encoder
```
panic: health check timeout: GET /healthz returned 404

stack: ...
```

eng-maya: Looks like livenessProbe path changed in the manifest accidentally (/live -> /healthz) but probe timeout is 1s and the new handler needs 500ms longer in warmup.

sre-zoe: Confirming: HPA kicked in hard after drain started, scaled pods from 3 -> 18 in 90s, some OOMs. HPA config targetCPU 5% (wrong), minReplicas 3, max 50.

infra-ali: Node drain started for rolling kernel update 08:17 UTC on 3 nodes; pods shifted and HPA reacted to CPU spike on sidecars. Some pods scheduled on older nodes with different network overlay and failed readiness.

support-tom: Customer-facing: Support telemetry shows ~20% of embedding requests 503/502 over the last 12min, concentrated in a few tenants using large batch embeddings. Two customers filed urgent tickets.

oncall-jay: OK immediate actions: 1) Pause rollout / toggle kill-switch for new encoder feature flag 2) Patch livenessProbe to tolerate warmup 3) Temporarily scale down HPA max and set min to 2 4) Rollback if needed. Who can flip the flag?

eng-maya: I can toggle the FF now. Hitting feature-flag service: `curl -X POST https://ff.internal/flags/new-encoder-rollout/toggle -d '{"enabled":false}'`

deploy-bot: Feature flag toggle accepted. new-encoder-rollout=false (reqid=ff-5201).

eng-maya: Patching deployment liveness probe (quick patch):
```
kubectl -n prod patch deploy encoder --type='json' -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/timeoutSeconds","value":3}]'
```

infra-ali: Pausing HPA autoscaling:
```
kubectl -n prod patch hpa encoder --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2,"maxReplicas":5}}'
```

eng-maya: Triggering rolling restart on encoder to pick up patch:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/encoder
```

oncall-jay: Executed restart, watching metrics. Support, please update customers that we're rolling mitigation and monitoring.

support-tom: Sent status update to impacted customers: "We're aware of degraded embedding performance in US-W, working a rollback and mitigation; ETA 15min."

incident-bot: metric update: 5xx rate back down to baseline in 4m after restart, p95 latency returned to normal. alert resolved (emb-5xx-5201) :white_check_mark:

eng-maya: Follow-up notes - root cause summary: accidental liveness timeout reduction + HPA target misconfiguration + coincident node drain amplified failures. Canary didn't fail fast because rollout policy was gradual and drain overlapped.

sre-zoe: Immediate postmortem actions: - Add CI lint to catch livenessProbe timeouts/path mismatches - Lock HPA target min to sane default via admission webhook - Change rollout policy to block if node drains are active (or detect cordon)

infra-ali: Action item: Add drain-aware admission or preflight to our rollout tool, and schedule kernel update with a shorter drain window.

support-tom: Customer impact summary: ~20% error rate for 12 minutes; two customers opened tickets, SLA exposure low but noticed. We'll follow up with affected accounts.

oncall-jay: Thanks team. I'm closing the page and creating an incident ticket for a full postmortem. If anyone finds additional data, drop it in #incident-postmortems. :thumbsup:
